title: Exact conservative component restriction on a total simplicial site
statement: Let $\mathcal C_\bullet$ be a simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] in small sites and morphisms of sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]: for $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ a morphism of sites $f_\varphi:\mathcal C_n\to\mathcal C_m$; the identity and composition laws may hold through specified isomorphisms $f_\varphi^{-1}f_{\psi}^{-1}\cong f_{\varphi\circ\psi}^{-1}$ for $\psi:[l]\to[m]$ (both sides functors $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_l)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_n)$), $f_{\mathrm{id}}^{-1}\cong\mathrm{id}$ satisfying the cocycle identities (equalities in the strict case). Let $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{total})$ be the category of systems $(F_n,F(\varphi))$ of sheaves $F_n$ on $\mathcal C_n$ and maps $F(\varphi):f_\varphi^{-1}F_m\to F_n$ compatible with identities and composition through these isomorphisms (in the strict case the sheaves on the total site), and $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{total})$ the analogous category of systems of abelian sheaves. For each $n$ let $r_n:\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{total})\to\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_n)$, $(F_k,F(\varphi))\mapsto F_n$. Then $r_n$ has an exact left adjoint $g_{n!}$, whose value on an abelian sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C_n$ has degree-$m$ component $\bigoplus_{\varphi:[n]\to[m]}f_\varphi^{-1}G$ with transition maps induced by the composition isomorphisms. Consequently each $r_n$ is exact, sends injective abelian sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions] to injective abelian sheaves and K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes (a cochain complex $I$ is K-injective if every morphism of cochain complexes $M\to I$ from a complex $M$ all of whose cohomology objects vanish is homotopic to zero), applying $r_n$ termwise, and the family $(r_n)_n$ is conservative.

proof.text: By the component description of sheaves on a simplicial site, a total sheaf is exactly a family $(F_m)_m$ of sheaves on $\mathcal C_m$ with transition maps $f_\varphi^{-1}F_m\to F_n$ satisfying the identity and composition compatibilities (with the specified coherent isomorphisms). Thus the functor induced by the inclusion of the $n$-th component is the stated restriction $r_n(F)=F_n$, and a morphism of total sheaves is an isomorphism whenever all its component maps are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09WF, lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site, and the system description immediately preceding it

proof.text: The inclusion of $\mathcal C_n$ into the total site is continuous and cocontinuous: coverings and fibre products of objects lying in degree $n$ are exactly those in $\mathcal C_n$. The induced topos morphism has inverse image $r_n$. For $G\in\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_n)$ define a system $g_{n!}G$ by $(g_{n!}G)_m=\bigoplus_{\varphi:[n]\to[m]}f_\varphi^{-1}G$; on a map $\psi:[m]\to[m_2]$, send the $\varphi$-summand through the coherent composition isomorphism $f_\psi^{-1}f_\varphi^{-1}G\cong f_{\psi\circ\varphi}^{-1}G$. Given a map $g_{n!}G\to F$, its components are adjoint to the composites $G\to F_n$ and the transition maps of $F$; conversely a map $G\to F_n$ gives these component maps. The two constructions are inverse by the component adjunctions and the coherence identities, so $g_{n!}\dashv r_n$ and the displayed formula holds.

source.place: Tag 09WG, lemma-restriction-to-components-site, cases A/B and proof of parts (1), (3), (5), (6)

proof.text: Each inverse-image functor $f_\varphi^{-1}$ is exact because $f_\varphi$ is a morphism of sites. Therefore each degree component of $g_{n!}$ is a direct sum of exact functors, hence exact; exactness of systems is checked componentwise under the description in Step 1. Consequently $g_{n!}$ is exact, and each $r_n$ is exact as asserted in the item. The same componentwise description shows conservativity: if every $r_n$ carries a morphism to an isomorphism, then every component map is an isomorphism, hence the original system morphism is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09WG, proof of part (7) and the componentwise system description in Tag 09WF

proof.text: For an injective abelian sheaf $I$ on the total site, the adjunction $g_{n!}\dashv r_n$ and exactness of $g_{n!}$ imply that $r_nI$ is injective: the exact functor $g_{n!}$ preserves monomorphisms, so the right adjoint sends injectives to injectives by [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] (equivalently, by Mathlib’s `CategoryTheory.Adjunction.map_injective`).

The same adjunction on complexes has exact left adjoint $g_{n!}$, so the generic right-adjoint K-injective preservation theorem [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies with $u=r_n$ and $v=g_{n!}$. It shows that applying $r_n$ termwise to any K-injective complex on the total site is K-injective on $\mathcal C_n$; in particular this includes the bounded-below K-injective complexes arising from injective resolutions. This completes all preservation and conservativity claims.
